## formal
Under Hypothesis (S), with the ten Majorana generators $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ of the five modes ($\gamma_{p}^{2} = 1$), the creation operators $v_{j} = \tfrac12(\gamma_{2j-1} + I\gamma_{2j})$, the mode numbers $n_{j} = v_{j}^{*}v_{j}$, the chirality $\Gamma = \prod_{j}(1 - 2n_{j})$ (the parity of the total mode number), the sixteen components of one generation the even part $V_{+}$ of $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, and the Majorana element $T = v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}v_{4}v_{5}$ of \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}; $I$ is the commuting unit of the module (the field theory's unit in the store's reading).
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The Klein twist carries no charge.)} For an even involution $k$ commuting with $I$, the twist $V_{k} = (1 + Ik)(1 + I)^{-1}$ of \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}(iv) is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$ with $p_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm k)$: a polynomial in $k$. So it exists on every graded module, whatever the number of components; it commutes with everything that commutes with $k$, in particular with every even element; every map that preserves the grading preserves it; and on an odd element $a$, $V_{k}aV_{k}^{-1} = -Iak$, which for two or more modes is not a multiple of $a$ nor in the span of the generators over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$. It is an order-four element with $V_{k}^{2} = k$, but it assigns no charge to the generators and no condition on the content can come from it.
\item \emph{(The pseudoscalar of the ten.)} $\omega = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\cdots\gamma_{10}$ satisfies $\omega^{2} = -1$, anticommutes with every $\gamma_{p}$ and commutes with all $45$ bivectors $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$, hence with the gauge algebra of every stage of the chain; and $\omega = I\,\Gamma$. So $\omega$ acts on all sixteen components of $V_{+}$ by the same unit $I$ (and by $-I$ on $V_{-}$): it is an order-four element whose square $-1$ is the grading of the field algebra, with one odd charge on every component, on fifteen components as on sixteen. It is the product of the five mode rotors, $\omega = \prod_{j}\exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})$, each generated by a bivector that preserves the split into slot and pair generators, so $\omega$ lies in the group generated by the Pati-Salam algebra (and by $\uu(5)$ and $\so(10)$).
\item \emph{(The Majorana element is odd under it.)} $T$ has grade five and $\omega T\omega^{-1} = -T$; on $V_{+}$ the bilinear form $B(\psi, T\varphi)$ of the cited claim changes sign under $\psi, \varphi \mapsto \omega\psi, \omega\varphi$. Hence $\omega$ is not in the group generated by the subalgebra that fixes $T$, the Standard Model algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)_{Y}$ of clause (2) of the cited claim, and a vev along $T$ breaks $\omega$ to $\omega^{2} = -1$. So in the stored chain $\omega$ is a gauge transformation at the Pati-Salam stage and above, and below it is broken to the grading by the same element that gives the neutral singlet its Majorana mass; it is an unbroken symmetry that is not a gauge transformation only if the Majorana term is absent.
\item \emph{(Arithmetic of signed counts; no anomaly statement is made.)} An order-four element with square $-1$ that commutes with the Standard Model algebra acts on each of the six multiplets of $V_{+}$, of dimensions $6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1$, by $\pm I$. The difference between the numbers of components with $+I$ and with $-I$ is $16$ for $\omega$, and takes the values $\pm 16$ and $0$ among others; on fifteen components (the neutral singlet removed) it is odd for every choice, so for an odd number of fifteen-component generations it is never divisible by $2$, and with the same uniform choice in each generation it is $15n_{g}$, divisible by $16$ only when $16$ divides $n_{g}$.
\end{enumerate}
Clause (4) is what a statement of the form "the difference must vanish modulo $16$" would give; that statement is literature cited from memory in the open problem and is neither imported nor derived here.

## technical
The open problem asks whether the store has an order-four symmetry whose square is the grading, and whether it could force sixteen components per generation. Two candidates are in the store and they behave differently. The Klein twist, which enters the geometric modular conjugations, is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$: the identity on the even part and the unit on the odd part. It is built from the grading alone, so every theory with a grading has it, with one component or with sixteen, and conjugation by it sends a generator $a$ to $-Iak$, a product with the full parity operator. It is not a transformation of the generators by a phase, and nothing about the content can be read from it.

The element that acts by one phase on all sixteen components is the pseudoscalar of the ten Majorana generators. Its square is $-1$, it commutes with every bivector, so with every gauge algebra of the chain, and it equals the unit times the chirality. It is the centre of the rotor group of the ten, a product of five quarter-period mode rotors, each inside the Pati-Salam algebra: at the Pati-Salam stage and above it is a gauge transformation, and the sixteenth component is already forced there by the multiplet structure. Below that stage the chain is broken by the element $T$, the product of the five creation operators, which is the Majorana term of the neutral singlet. $T$ has odd grade, so the pseudoscalar anticommutes with it: the same element that gives the singlet its mass breaks the order-four element to its square. The only reading in which the order-four element is an unbroken symmetry that is not a gauge transformation is one without the Majorana term, against the stored premise that the term is realised. The last clause records the counting that the literature's modulo-16 statement would use, as arithmetic: fifteen components always give an odd signed count.

## lay
Some consistency arguments in particle physics use a symmetry that returns to the starting point only after four steps, and whose second step is the sign flip of all fermions; such a symmetry can require the fermions of one generation to come in sixteens. The store was thought to contain a symmetry of this kind in a twist used for its vacuum states. This result shows that the twist is built from the sign flip alone and so says nothing about how many fermions there are. A second four-step element does treat all sixteen fermions alike, but in the series' chain of symmetry breaking it is either part of the gauge symmetry, or it is broken by the very term that makes the sixteenth fermion, the heavy neutrino partner, massive. So within the stored chain it cannot be used to argue for sixteen rather than fifteen, unless that mass term is absent.

## one-liner
Under Hypothesis (S), the Klein twist is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$, a polynomial in the grading that assigns no charge to generators; the pseudoscalar $\omega$ of the ten Majoranas has $\omega^{2} = -1$, equals $I\Gamma$ (one odd charge on all sixteen), lies in the Pati-Salam group, and the Majorana element satisfies $\omega T\omega^{-1} = -T$, so a vev along $T$ breaks it to the grading.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(1).} Since $k^{2} = 1$ and $I^{2} = -1$ commute, $(1 + I)^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 - I)$ and $(1 + Ik)(1 - I) = 1 + k - I(1 - k)$, so $V_{k} = p_{+} - Ip_{-}$; this is the element of \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}(iv), where $V_{k}^{2} = k$ is proved. Being a polynomial in $k$ with coefficients in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, it is defined whenever $k$ is, commutes with whatever commutes with $k$ and $I$, and is carried to itself by every map that fixes $k$ and $I$. For odd $a$, $p_{\pm}a = ap_{\mp}$, so $V_{k}aV_{k}^{-1} = (p_{+} - Ip_{-})a(p_{+} + Ip_{-}) = I(p_{+}ap_{-} - p_{-}ap_{+}) = Ia(p_{-} - p_{+}) = -Iak$. For two modes with generators $e_{1}, \dots, e_{4}$ and $k = e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$, $-Ie_{1}k = -Ie_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$, a product of three generators, not a combination of generators (checked in $\Cl(4,1)$, where the pseudoscalar is a central unit: the result has grade two, while $ce_{j}$ and $cIe_{j}$ have grades one and four). With more modes $k$ contains more factors.

\emph{(2).} $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{10\cdot 9/2} = -1$. Moving $\gamma_{p}$ through $\omega$ passes nine other generators, so $\omega\gamma_{p} = -\gamma_{p}\omega$, and $\omega$ commutes with products of two generators. From $v_{j}^{*}v_{j} = \tfrac12(1 + I\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})$, $\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j} = -I(2n_{j} - 1) = I(1 - 2n_{j})$, so $\omega = I^{5}\prod_{j}(1 - 2n_{j}) = I\Gamma$. On $V_{+}$, $\Gamma = 1$ and $\omega = I$. Since $(\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})^{2} = -1$, $\exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j}) = \gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j}$, and the two generators of one mode are both slot generators or both pair generators, so each of these bivectors is among the $21$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}. The statement about fifteen components: removing one component of $V_{+}$ does not change the action on the others.

\emph{(3).} $T$ is a product of five elements each linear in the generators, and the five pairs are disjoint, so $T$ is of grade five (\claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}); $\omega$ anticommutes with every element of odd grade by (2), so $\omega T\omega^{-1} = -T$. On $V_{+}$, $\omega = I$ and $B$ is bilinear over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, so $B(\omega\psi, T\omega\varphi) = I^{2}B(\psi, T\varphi) = -B(\psi, T\varphi)$. Every element of the group generated by the subalgebra fixing $T$ commutes with $T$; $\omega$ does not, so it is not in that group; that subalgebra is the Standard Model algebra, and a vev along $T$ breaks Pati-Salam to it, by clauses (2) and (3) of the cited claim. The bit of the neutral singlet is fixed at the stages that leave $\uu(5)$ (\claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}), which is where $\omega$ is a gauge transformation.

\emph{(4).} The six multiplets of $V_{+}$ under the Standard Model algebra are pairwise inequivalent, so an element commuting with the algebra is a scalar of $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ on each, and with square $-1$ the scalar is $\pm I$. The signed sums $\pm 6 \pm 3 \pm 3 \pm 2 \pm 1 \pm 1$ include $16$, $-16$ and $0$ (for instance $6 + 2 - 3 - 3 - 1 - 1$). The sum of $6, 3, 3, 2, 1$ is $15$, odd, and changing a sign changes a signed sum by an even number, so every signed sum for fifteen components is odd; a sum of an odd number of odd integers is odd. $15n_{g} \equiv -n_{g} \pmod{16}$.

check_py:
"""synthesis.order-four-elements-with-square-the-grading-and-the-majorana-element: exact checks.

Two order-four elements whose square is a grading occur in the store. (a) The Klein twist
V = (1 + I k)(1 + I)^{-1} of an even involution k (the grading) with the unit I: checked in Cl(4,1), where
e_1 .. e_4 are the Majorana generators of two modes, the pseudoscalar I is central with I^2 = -1, and
k = e_1e_2e_3e_4. (b) The pseudoscalar omega of the ten Majorana generators of the five modes, in Cl(10,0);
elements of the complexified algebra are pairs (A, B) for A + I B with I a commuting unit. Checks:
  (1) V = p_+ - I p_-, V^2 = k, V commutes with every even element, and Ad_V(e_1) = -I e_1 k is not in the span
      of the generators over span{1, I}: the twist assigns no charge to a generator;
  (2) omega^2 = -1, omega anticommutes with the ten generators and commutes with the 45 bivectors; it is the
      product of the five mode rotors exp((pi/2) e_{2j-1}e_{2j}) = e_{2j-1}e_{2j};
  (3) omega = I Gamma with Gamma the product of (1 - 2 n_j): the same unit I on every even state;
  (4) the Majorana element T = v_1 v_2 v_3 v_4 v_5 is of grade five and omega T omega^{-1} = -T;
  (5) signed sums of the multiplet dimensions (6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1) and (6, 3, 3, 2, 1).
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import GA
from tp_premise import premise

MODES = 5
GENS = 2 * MODES
SQ10 = GA.sig(GENS, 0)
SIXTEEN = (6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1)      # (2,3), (1,3bar), (1,3bar), (2,1), (1,1), (1,1): the sixteen of one generation
FIFTEEN = (6, 3, 3, 2, 1)         # without the neutral singlet
MODULUS = 16


def check_klein_twist_is_a_polynomial_in_the_grading():
    premise("synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics")
    sq = GA.sig(4, 1)
    e = [GA.gen(i) for i in range(5)]
    one = GA.sc(F(1))

    def prod(*xs):
        out = one
        for x in xs:
            out = GA.mul(out, x, sq)
        return out

    I = prod(*e)                                                # central pseudoscalar of Cl(4,1)
    k = prod(e[0], e[1], e[2], e[3])                            # the grading of the two-mode algebra
    assert GA.eq(prod(I, I), GA.neg(one)) and GA.eq(prod(k, k), one)
    for g in e:
        assert GA.commutes(I, g, sq)
    for g in e[:4]:
        assert GA.anticommutes(k, g, sq)                        # generators are odd
    half = F(1, 2)
    V = GA.scal(half, prod(GA.add(one, prod(I, k)), GA.sub(one, I)))        # (1 + I k)(1 + I)^{-1}
    Vinv = GA.scal(half, prod(GA.sub(one, prod(I, k)), GA.add(one, I)))
    p_plus = GA.scal(half, GA.add(one, k))
    p_minus = GA.scal(half, GA.sub(one, k))
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, Vinv), one)
    assert GA.eq(V, GA.sub(p_plus, prod(I, p_minus)))           # V = p_+ - I p_-: a polynomial in k
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, V), k)                                 # order four, square the grading
    for a in range(4):
        for b in range(a + 1, 4):
            assert GA.commutes(V, prod(e[a], e[b]), sq)         # commutes with every even element
    ad = prod(V, e[0], Vinv)
    assert GA.eq(ad, GA.neg(prod(I, e[0], k)))                  # Ad_V(e_1) = -I e_1 k
    grades = set(len(b) for b, c in ad.items() if c != 0)
    assert grades == {2}                                        # e_1 e_5 up to sign: not c e_j or c I e_j (grades 1, 4)
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, V, e[0], Vinv, Vinv), GA.neg(e[0]))    # Ad_V^2 is the grading automorphism
    return True


def blade(*idx):
    out = GA.sc(F(1))
    for i in idx:
        out = GA.mul(out, GA.gen(i), SQ10)
    return out


def check_pseudoscalar_of_the_ten_generators():
    premise("standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are")
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    one = GA.sc(F(1))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(omega, omega, SQ10), GA.neg(one))       # omega^2 = -1
    for p in range(GENS):
        assert GA.anticommutes(omega, GA.gen(p), SQ10)
    count = 0
    for p in range(GENS):
        for q in range(p + 1, GENS):
            assert GA.commutes(omega, blade(p, q), SQ10)
            count += 1
    assert count == 45
    # omega is the product of the five mode rotors: (e_a e_b)^2 = -1, so exp((pi/2) e_a e_b) = e_a e_b
    rot = one
    for j in range(MODES):
        r = blade(2 * j, 2 * j + 1)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(r, r, SQ10), GA.neg(one))
        rot = GA.mul(rot, r, SQ10)
    assert GA.eq(rot, omega)
    return True


def cmul(x, y):
    """(A + I B)(C + I D) with I a commuting unit, I^2 = -1."""
    A, B = x
    C, D = y
    return (GA.sub(GA.mul(A, C, SQ10), GA.mul(B, D, SQ10)), GA.add(GA.mul(A, D, SQ10), GA.mul(B, C, SQ10)))


ZERO = GA.sc(F(0))


def mode_ops(j):
    half = F(1, 2)
    a, b = GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1)
    v = (GA.scal(half, a), GA.scal(half, b))                    # v_j = (e_a + I e_b)/2
    vd = (GA.scal(half, a), GA.scal(-half, b))                  # its adjoint (e_a - I e_b)/2
    return v, vd


def check_pseudoscalar_is_the_unit_times_the_chirality():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    one = (GA.sc(F(1)), ZERO)
    gamma = one
    for j in range(MODES):
        v, vd = mode_ops(j)
        n = cmul(vd, v)                                         # the number operator of mode j
        assert GA.eq(cmul(n, n)[0], n[0]) and GA.eq(cmul(n, n)[1], n[1])      # a projection
        factor = (GA.sub(one[0], GA.scal(F(2), n[0])), GA.neg(GA.scal(F(2), n[1])))
        gamma = cmul(gamma, factor)
    g2 = cmul(gamma, gamma)
    assert GA.eq(g2[0], one[0]) and GA.is_zero(g2[1])           # Gamma^2 = 1
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    i_gamma = (GA.neg(gamma[1]), gamma[0])                      # I Gamma
    assert GA.eq(i_gamma[0], omega) and GA.is_zero(i_gamma[1])  # omega = I Gamma: the unit I on every even state
    return True


def check_majorana_element_is_odd_under_the_pseudoscalar():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    premise("synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5")
    T = (GA.sc(F(1)), ZERO)
    for j in range(MODES):
        T = cmul(T, mode_ops(j)[0])
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    omega_inv = GA.neg(omega)
    for part in T:
        assert not GA.is_zero(part)
        assert set(len(b) for b, c in part.items() if c != 0) == {MODES}      # grade five
        conj = GA.mul(GA.mul(omega, part, SQ10), omega_inv, SQ10)
        assert GA.eq(conj, GA.neg(part))                        # omega T omega^{-1} = -T
    # the mode bivectors: [sum_j e_{2j-1}e_{2j}, T] = c I T with c = 2 * MODES up to the sign convention of v_j,
    # so T has charge 2 under each mode rotor, and every difference of two mode bivectors commutes with T
    def comm(X, part):
        return GA.sub(GA.mul(X, part, SQ10), GA.mul(part, X, SQ10))
    mode_biv = [GA.mul(GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1), SQ10) for j in range(MODES)]
    total = GA.add(*mode_biv)
    i_T = (GA.neg(T[1]), T[0])                                   # I T
    c_re, c_im = comm(total, T[0]), comm(total, T[1])
    weight = 2 * MODES
    plus = GA.eq(c_re, GA.scal(F(weight), i_T[0])) and GA.eq(c_im, GA.scal(F(weight), i_T[1]))
    minus = GA.eq(c_re, GA.scal(F(-weight), i_T[0])) and GA.eq(c_im, GA.scal(F(-weight), i_T[1]))
    assert plus or minus
    for j in range(MODES):
        for l in range(j + 1, MODES):
            d = GA.sub(mode_biv[j], mode_biv[l])
            assert GA.is_zero(comm(d, T[0])) and GA.is_zero(comm(d, T[1]))
    return True


def signed_sums(dims):
    out = []
    for mask in range(2 ** len(dims)):
        out.append(sum(d if (mask >> i) & 1 else -d for i, d in enumerate(dims)))
    return out


def check_signed_dimension_sums_for_fifteen_and_sixteen():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    s16 = signed_sums(SIXTEEN)
    s15 = signed_sums(FIFTEEN)
    assert sum(SIXTEEN) == MODULUS and sum(FIFTEEN) == MODULUS - 1
    assert all(s % 2 == 1 for s in s15)                         # fifteen: every signed sum is odd
    assert sorted(set(s % MODULUS for s in s16 if s % MODULUS == 0)) == [0]
    zero16 = [s for s in s16 if s % MODULUS == 0]
    assert MODULUS in zero16 and -MODULUS in zero16 and 0 in zero16          # uniform, and balanced choices
    # three fifteen-component generations: no choice of signs gives a multiple of 16, or of 2
    vals15 = sorted(set(s15))
    for a in vals15:
        for b in vals15:
            for c in vals15:
                assert (a + b + c) % 2 == 1
    # two generations can cancel (opposite signs), so the obstruction is for odd numbers of generations
    assert any((a + b) % MODULUS == 0 for a in vals15 for b in vals15)
    # with the same uniform choice in each generation: 15 n_g = 0 mod 16 first at n_g = 16
    assert [g for g in range(1, MODULUS + 1) if (15 * g) % MODULUS == 0] == [MODULUS]
    return True
